paper_id: Why Do Neural Dialog Systems Generate Short and Meaningless Replies_ A Comparison between Dialog and Translation
title: Why Do Neural Dialog Systems Generate Short and Meaningless Replies? A Comparison between Dialog and Translation
motivation: Neural dialog systems generate useless universal replies like 'I don't know' and 'Me too', degrading real-world conversation systems.
problem_framing: Hypothesis: dialog's unaligned conditional distribution (multiple equally plausible replies) causes Seq2Seq deficiency.
key_insight: Shuffling translation pairs mimics the unaligned property; this reproduces short/generic reply phenomenon in translation.
method_signature: Shuffle translation source-target pairs at varying rates to artificially construct unaligned datasets.
evaluation_criteria: BLEU scores, reply length, negative log-probability, entropy, and hidden-state time-step correlation.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: 100% shuffled data shows inconsistent encoder correlation (.99) but decoder only .85; no good explanation provided.
evidence_for_taste: shows evidence that the unaligned property could be one reason
impossible to construct exactly the same scenario
more suitable to applications where the source and target information is aligned
thinking_moves: 从现象(通用回复)反推根本假设(分布多峰导致模型学习退化)
通过数据打乱人工构造目标分布多峰,实现可控实验
控制单一变量(对齐度)观察性能变化,验证因果假说
跨任务迁移实验范式(translation→dialog)揭示通用学习困境
extraction_notes: Zhi Jin appears as senior author (last position in PKU affiliation group). Venue is arXiv preprint (no formal venue). Both dialog and translation models use identical architectures for fair comparison.
